shared_elements: shallow low-relief curvilinear grooves forming abstract motifs
broad arc / crescent or U-shaped band
motifs spread over a convex, sculpted stone surface (back/upper surface of a carved block)
justification: Both surfaces carry the same repertoire of shallow, smooth-edged relief motifs — broad crescent/U-shaped arcs, paired vertical bars and forked linear elements — laid out as isolated, non-overlapping signs across a rounded sculpted surface, and the carving conventions (rounded ridges, no infill, schematic outline-only forms) are effectively identical; A's motifs plausibly belong to the same sign system as the arcs, rings and paired uprights on B. The chief difference is that B additionally displays clearly readable figurative content — a sculpted head with facial features and creature/face-bearing elements above the arcs — whereas A, seen only as a fragmentary detail, shows purely abstract curvilinear signs with no identifiable figure, so the specific combination cannot be confirmed.
